findings.source_passage: Such things may seem incredible; but, however wondrous, they are true. Nor is the history of fanatics half so striking in respect to the measureless self-deception of the fanatic himself, as his measureless power of deceiving and bedevilling so many others.
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing Gabriel's hold over the crew, near end of his backstory
findings.why_it_matters: This is Melville's authorial aside on fanaticism—rhetorically distinctive and thematically central to the chapter's meditation on religious mania and mass credulity; its balanced paradox ('self-deception' vs. 'power of deceiving others') is signature Melvillean moralizing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-sentence aside verbatim or in near-verbatim form after the description of the crew's homage to Gabriel.

findings.source_passage: He published his manifesto, whereby he set himself forth as the deliverer of the isles of the sea and vicar-general of all Oceanica.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'deliverer of the isles of the sea and vicar-general of all Oceanica' is rhetorically flamboyant and interpretively important—it frames Gabriel's grandiosity in apocalyptic/colonial terms. The draft reduces it to 'vicar-general of Oceanica,' losing 'deliverer of the isles of the sea.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full phrase: 'deliverer of the isles of the sea and vicar-general of all Oceanica.'

findings.source_passage: It is well to parenthesize here, that of the fatal accidents in the Sperm-Whale Fishery, this kind is perhaps almost as frequent as any. Sometimes, nothing is injured but the man who is thus annihilated; oftener the boat's bow is knocked off, or the thigh-board, in which the headsman stands, is torn from its place and accompanies the body.
findings.why_it_matters: The narratorial parenthesis is a characteristic Melvillean intrusion—its casual-documentary tone ('it is well to parenthesize here') is a voice-establishing gesture. The draft collapses it to a brief clause, erasing the rhetorical texture and the detail about thigh-boards.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical paragraph in near-verbatim form, including the word 'annihilated' and the thigh-board detail, to preserve the narratorial voice.

findings.source_passage: Of such a letter, Death himself might well have been the post-boy.
findings.why_it_matters: This is among the sharpest epigram-level sentences in the chapter—widely recognized as a signature Melvillean one-liner that delivers the chapter's irony in a single image. The draft notes the letter is 'as if Death had been post-boy,' which is a near-paraphrase but strips the syntactic precision and the 'might well have been' modal.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence verbatim: 'Of such a letter, Death himself might well have been the post-boy.'

findings.source_passage: Here be it said, that like the vessels of military marines, the ships of the American Whale Fleet have each a private signal; all which signals being collected in a book with the names of the respective vessels attached, every captain is provided with it.
findings.why_it_matters: The documentary aside on the whale-fleet signal system is a minor voice-establishing digression typical of Melville's encyclopedic register; its omission is a small loss of that texture, though not a critical one.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider adding a brief clause noting the American whale-fleet's private signal system to preserve the documentary register.

summary: The draft loses four passages of meaningful signature weight: the authorial epigram on fanaticism's self-deception, the parenthetical on fatal fishery accidents (both voice-establishing Melvillean intrusions), the precise 'Death himself might well have been the post-boy' one-liner, and a partial erasure of the 'deliverer of the isles of the sea' formulation—three of these rise to medium severity, triggering regeneration.
